⊢=𐑦: The Hodge conjecture posits that the global cohomological structure (bulk) is entirely determined by algebraic cycles (boundary/surface), implying a scale-collapse where the surface carries the full interior content.
⊞=𐑙: The Hodge conjecture posits a symmetric correspondence where every rational Hodge class of type (p,p) is exactly represented by an algebraic cycle, implying an equal pairing between the cohomology and cycle sides.
◻=𐑭: The Hodge conjecture posits that rational Hodge classes are algebraic cycles, which are topologically stable and characterized by integer cohomology classes that cannot be continuously deformed to zero without crossing a singularity.
⊙=⊙: The system is at the threshold where the cohomology and cycle sides fuse to realize every rational class, indicating maximal sensitivity and scale-free correlations characteristic of criticality.

≺=𐑹: The statement that the cycle class map composes to the identity (μ∘δ=id) and realizes every rational class as a combination of cycles corresponds to the exact Z2 symmetry at criticality described in option 5.
⋈=𐑐: The Hodge conjecture posits a deterministic, geometry-enforcing correspondence where every rational Hodge class is exactly realized by algebraic cycles, implying near-certainty in the mapping.
⊤=𐑧: The Hodge conjecture posits a rigid structural constraint where rational classes are locked into algebraic cycles, representing a high kinetic barrier that prevents free rearrangement without specific geometric driving.
∈=𐑔: The Hodge conjecture posits a global correspondence where every rational cohomology class across the entire manifold is realized by algebraic cycles, indicating a scale-free propagation of the cycle class map.
∋=𐑝: The logic requires the simultaneous presence of both the cohomology side and the cycle side to fuse back and compose the identity, satisfying the conjunctive condition.
